article.title: Too Big to Fire? Jensen Huang Is Back at Nvidia; Questions Loom Over AI Boom & U.S.-China Relations
article.content: Nvidia stock prices surged over 30% on Monday as the chip maker reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO . Huang had stepped down earlier in November amid reports he had multiple extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of spying for China. Huang and Nvidia have been central to the AI boom, and the leadership turmoil had erased trillions in value from the U.S. stock market. President Donald Trump acknowledged he had encouraged the company’s board to bring Huang back. “The fact that our markets are so over-indexed on the AI trade, that something like three-fourths of gains in the [S&P 500] this past year have been AI-related, is unsustainable,” says Aya Ibrahim, senior fellow for economic and national security at the AI Now Institute. We also speak with organizer and researcher Tobita Chow, who says Huang’s “spy scandal” that led to his ouster is part of a larger effort by anti-China figures in the U.S. national security establishment to escalate tensions between the countries. “The national security leadership in both parties in D.C. has been greatly frustrated with President Trump, who has over the past year pursued policies to maintain very warm relations with Xi Jinping,” says Chow, who notes that Secretary of State Marco Rubio is one of the “chief” frustrated China hawks in the administration.
